issues.title: docs/index.md still tells the reader bare /gogo:done "opens the work board" - the exact enumeration surface code-review-standards.md #1 names
issues.description: docs/index.md:83 (the quick-reference command table) still reads: "Ship one report-complete feature, or several as ONE merged release entry (no slug opens the work board)." That is false after slice 1: bare /gogo:done now ships in chat and board.py is deleted (git rm'd). Every other surface was synced (README.md, docs/commands.md, docs/flow.md, docs/architecture.md, skills/gogo/SKILL.md, skills/gogo-status/SKILL.md, commands/done.md), so index.md is the one straggler - and it is the FIRST page a reader lands on. code-review-standards.md check #1 calls this surface out by name: "A doc-sync sweep must enumerate all of docs/*.md - including the docs/index.md quick-reference table - never just the plan's hand-listed subset (the surface REV-001 caught slipping through in 0.8.0)." The plan's checklist item 7 hand-listed only commands/flow/architecture, and the build followed the list rather than the standard. Severity major per the severity guide ("an enumeration left out of sync"). The new TestNoInteractiveBoardInSkills guard cannot catch it: it scans skills/*/SKILL.md + commands/*.md only, and the stale sentence contains none of its three banned tokens.

issues.title: Sessions panel `R` with zero drivable work items opens a picker whose only option is Cancel - no named refusal (Diagnosability / FR4.2)
issues.description:
cli/internal/tui/session_ops.go:437-462 (startReassignPicker) builds the target options by filtering out every orchestrator.TerminalStatus feature. When a board has NO non-terminal item - a repo where everything has shipped, which is the steady state of a mature repo, and the panel deliberately lists sessions from OTHER repos too - the options slice degrades to just the Cancel sentinel. Verified by driving the model (all fixture features forced to `shipped`): pressing S then R renders
  `Re-assign gogo-go-inprogress onto which work item?` / `> Cancel`
and Enter lands back on the panel with status `cancelled`. The user pressed a documented key, got a form with nothing to choose, and no explanation. FR4.2's own words are "a refusal explains, a missing row puzzles (Diagnosability)", and non-functional-requirements.md's Diagnosability bar says a refusal must carry its unblock. The card-anchored twin (adoptFeature, session_ops.go:278-299) already refuses up front for its analogous empty cases (no tmux / no live session); the panel's R has no equivalent guard. updateSessions' `K` has the same shape but degrades harmlessly (a confirm on a real session).
issues.proposed_solution: AGENT-FIXABLE. In cli/internal/tui/update.go's `case "R"` of updateSessions (or as an early return in startReassignPicker), count the drivable features first and refuse when the count is 0 - e.g. `m.statusBlocked("no drivable work item to re-assign onto - every card here is shipped/aborted; K closes the session, or plan a new item first")` - instead of opening a Cancel-only picker. Add a subtest to cli/internal/tui/sessions_panel_test.go that forces every fixture feature terminal, presses S then R, and asserts mode stays modeSessions with statusLevelWarn and the named reason (the probe above is the fixture).
issues.fix_summary: updateSessions R refuses with a named reason when hasDrivableFeature() is false (shared predicate with the picker filter); subtest forces every fixture feature terminal and asserts panel + amber + wording. VERIFIED round 2: update.go:422-434 guards before startReassignPicker; session_ops.go:434-441 hasDrivableFeature() uses the SAME `f != nil && !orchestrator.TerminalStatus(f.Status)` predicate as the picker filter, so refusal and row set cannot disagree; the refusal's remedy (`K closes the session, or plan a new item first`) is targeted, satisfying standard #12. MUTATION re-run in a sandbox copy (guard condition forced to `if false`): TestSessionsPanelReassign/zero_drivable_items_refuses_with_a_named_reason FAILS ("zero-target R left the panel (mode=3)"). The guard bites.

issues.title: TestSessionsPanelCursorClamps does not bite: deleting the production tick-clamp keeps the whole tui suite green
issues.description: cli/internal/tui/sessions_panel_test.go:244-263 claims to cover FR3.4 ("the list is live - a session tick that shrinks it clamps the cursor instead of pointing past the end"), but it asserts through `m.focusedSession()`, which itself clamps on read (session_ops.go:418-423). Mutation-verified: deleting `m.clampSessIdx()` from Update's `case sessionsMsg` (update.go) leaves `go test ./internal/tui/` fully green, including this test. The production clamp is NOT dead code - without it a shrunken list leaves m.sessIdx past the end, and the next `up` keypress computes clamp(sessIdx-1, 0, len-1) from the stale index, so the first `up` after a shrink is silently swallowed. This is code-review-standards.md check #11(c) - "a test passed for a weaker reason than it claimed" - and test-strategy.md's assertion-that-isn't family.
issues.proposed_solution: AGENT-FIXABLE. In TestSessionsPanelCursorClamps, assert the FIELD the handler writes, not the clamped read: after sending the shrinking sessionsMsg, add `if m.sessIdx != 0 { t.Errorf("sessIdx = %d after the list shrank to 1, want 0 (the tick must clamp, not just the read)", m.sessIdx) }`. Optionally also press `up` afterwards and assert the cursor is still row 0. Re-run the mutation (no-op the clampSessIdx call in the sessionsMsg case) and confirm the test now fails.
issues.fix_summary: TestSessionsPanelCursorClamps asserts m.sessIdx == 0 (the field the handler writes); mutation re-run - no-opping the tick clamp now fails the test. VERIFIED round 2: sessions_panel_test.go:316-321 asserts the field. MUTATION re-run in the sandbox (the `m.clampSessIdx()` call in Update's `case sessionsMsg` commented out): TestSessionsPanelCursorClamps FAILS with "sessIdx = 2 after the list shrank to 1, want 0". The production clamp is now pinned.

issues.title: The `pendingKillSession` leg of cancelForm's returnMode list is unpinned - deleting it keeps the whole tui suite green
issues.description: The plan calls out the five-place pending* form contract explicitly (field decl / StateCompleted dispatch / cancelForm returnMode / cancelForm clear / formPreservesSelection) and warns "Miss the third and Esc bounces to the board instead of back to the panel". All five places are correctly wired for BOTH new fields - but only `pendingReassign` is guarded. Mutation-verified: deleting `|| m.pendingKillSession != ""` from update.go:633's returnMode condition leaves `go test -count=1 ./internal/tui/` fully green (I re-ran the whole package with templates/ present), while the user-visible effect is real: Esc-aborting the panel's `K` confirm would then land on the board instead of back in the panel. The panel-K test (sessions_panel_test.go:211-223) only exercises the bare-Enter COMPLETION path (finishKillSession), never the Esc/abort path (cancelForm). By contrast the reassign leg IS pinned - deleting `|| m.pendingReassign != ""` fails TestSessionsPanelReassign/cancel_returns_to_the_panel. This is code-review-standards.md #11(b) ("a wiring was named in the plan, shipped, and had no test that bites") and #12's "pin the wirings, not just the producer".
issues.proposed_solution: AGENT-FIXABLE. Add a subtest to TestSessionsPanelKill mirroring the reassign one: press S, press K, send tea.KeyEsc via keyPress, then assert `m.mode == modeSessions` and `len(rk.calls) == 0`. While there, add the Cancel-OPTION arm of the panel's R (select the Cancel row and submit) so both cancel doors the plan names ("pickerOrigin on Cancel *and* Esc") are covered. Verify each new assertion by re-running the corresponding one-leg mutation on cancelForm's returnMode condition.
issues.fix_summary: Two new cancel-door subtests: panel-K Esc-abort (pins the pendingKillSession returnMode leg - mutation re-run fails) and the R picker's Cancel OPTION (wrap-up k -> Enter). VERIFIED round 2: sessions_panel_test.go:270-282 (esc-abort) + :208-224 (Cancel option). MUTATION re-run in the sandbox (dropped `|| m.pendingKillSession != ""` from cancelForm's returnMode line ONLY, leaving the clear + formPreservesSelection legs intact): TestSessionsPanelKill/esc-abort_returns_to_the_panel_and_kills_nothing FAILS ("landed in mode=0, want the panel"). The named leg is pinned. Probed the Cancel-option subtest too: it really lands on the Cancel row (status "cancelled", level OK), so huh's wrap assumption holds - but see REV-010 for the reason-assertion gap that arm still leaves.

issues.title: gogo-session-update's "cap at 48 chars" is ambiguous about WHAT is capped - a whole-name reading mints a name neither SessionMatchesSlug candidate accepts (FR10)
issues.description: skills/gogo-session-update/SKILL.md:77-80 states the name transform as: "`gogo-<action>-<sanitized-slug>` - lowercase, `[^a-z0-9-]+` -> `-`, trim `-`, cap at 48 chars." The Go producer caps the LABEL, not the name: cli/internal/launch/launch.go:96 `MaxSessionLabel = 48` is applied by sanitizeLabel (launch.go:749-771) to the slug component only, and it cuts on the last `-` boundary ONLY when that boundary is past MaxSessionLabel/2, else it takes a hard cut and TrimRights the dash. The skill omits both facts. Read as a whole-name cap, any slug of 39+ characters (`gogo-plan-` is 10 chars) yields a TRUNCATED slug component - and a truncated slug matches NEITHER candidate base SessionMatchesSlug tries (launch.go:808-826 keeps the capped and the UNCAPPED label, not an arbitrary truncation), so the renamed session binds to nothing: the board shows it as unbound and the per-source cap stops counting it. That is degrading to WRONG, which non-functional-requirements.md forbids, and it is the one risk the plan's own FR10 ("the three doors agree") exists to close. Not hypothetical-far: this repo's longest live slug is `plans-tab-launch-diagnostics-and-view` at 37 characters, two below the threshold.
issues.proposed_solution: AGENT-FIXABLE. Reword step 5 of skills/gogo-session-update/SKILL.md to pin the cap to the label and name its source, e.g.: "cap the SANITIZED SLUG (not the whole name) at 48 chars - `launch.MaxSessionLabel`; when the cut lands past char 24, cut back to the last `-` and trim it, else keep the hard cut. For a real work-item slug (already kebab, <48) this is simply `gogo-<action>-<slug>`." Keep the existing note that the transform is a near-identity for real slugs so the step stays short.
issues.fix_summary: Step 5 pins the cap to the SANITIZED SLUG (launch.MaxSessionLabel) with the past-24 dash-boundary rule, and states the transform is a no-op for a real <48 kebab slug. VERIFIED round 2 against launch.go:750-770: the prose ("cap the sanitized slug (the label - NOT the whole name) at 48 chars (launch.MaxSessionLabel); when that cut lands past char 24, cut back to the last `-` and trim it, else keep the hard cut") matches sanitizeLabel exactly - including the equivalence that the else-branch can never end in a dash (a trailing dash at index 47 would itself be a boundary > 24), so omitting TrimRight there is not a divergence. The residual is the bash snippet three lines below; filed separately as REV-011 rather than reopening this one.

issues.title: The plan's phase-⑤ reconcile list misses four surfaces that still instruct readers to use the deleted assets/kanban/board.py
issues.description: board.py is git rm'd, but four live surfaces still describe it as present, and only three of them (tech-stack.md, non-functional-requirements.md, project-knowledge.md) are on the plan's item-19 reconcile list - so the ⑤ sweep as planned will leave the rest stale. Missing: (1) .gogo/knowledge/testing-tools.md:37 - tells a tester to run `python3 assets/kanban/board.py --selftest` (and `--headless --ship a,b`); (2) .gogo/knowledge/test-strategy.md:49 and :63 - the same selftest instruction plus a `tmux new-session ... python3 assets/kanban/board.py --index <idx>` live-TUI recipe; (3) .gogo/knowledge/coding-rules.md:41 - the "Vendored executable assets (since 0.7.0)" rule whose only example is board.py; (4) .gitignore:22-25 - the comment "assets/kanban/board.py is vendored source" plus the now-dead `__pycache__/` / `*.pyc` entries. Knowledge files are always-read context for every pipeline worker, so a stale instruction to run a deleted file is worse than ordinary doc drift. Raising it here (not as an implement-phase blocker) because the plan deliberately scoped knowledge reconcile to ⑤ - the defect is that the ⑤ list is incomplete.
issues.proposed_solution: AGENT-FIXABLE (at phase ⑤, not implement). Extend the reconcile set to testing-tools.md, test-strategy.md, coding-rules.md and .gitignore: drop the board.py selftest/live-TUI recipes from the two test docs; either delete coding-rules.md's "Vendored executable assets" section or restate it generically (the rule may still be worth keeping - it now has no live example, which is a decision to state in one line); and in .gitignore either delete the __pycache__/*.pyc block with its comment or reword the comment to say no vendored python ships today. Then grep the tree once more for `board.py` / `assets/kanban` and confirm only docs/cli-contract.md's deliberate 0.33.0 "no longer written" note remains.
issues.fix_summary: PARTIAL in round 2: .gitignore comment rewritten (no vendored python ships today). The three .gogo/knowledge surfaces (testing-tools, test-strategy, coding-rules) are the phase-⑤ reconcile, per the finding's own note. ROUND-2 CHECK: the .gitignore half is done and reads correctly (.gitignore:22-23). Re-grep confirms the remaining live hits are EXACTLY the knowledge set - testing-tools.md:37,45 · test-strategy.md:49,63,72 · coding-rules.md:41,46 - plus the three surfaces already on the plan's item-19 list (tech-stack.md:23,74 · project-knowledge.md:118,133,142 · non-functional-requirements.md:20,61-63). No product or doc surface outside .gogo/knowledge/ still points at board.py, so keeping this open and ⑤-scoped is correct; it must not silently drop off the ⑤ sweep. Worth folding into the same ⑤ pass: tech-stack.md's test-function count still reads "559 as of 0.32.0".

issues.title: The new per-case anti-vacuity floor for updateSessions is half the real key count, and its two comments contradict each other
issues.description: cli/internal/tui/key_help_sync_test.go:109 sets `floor: 4` for the updateSessions case with the comment "up/down/jk + R + K + esc/q - a smaller switch, its own floor", while the block comment at :119-120 says "updateSessions only ~8". The parser counts KEYS, not key groups: updateSessions handles esc, q, up, k, down, j, R, K = 8. FR6.2 asked for a per-case floor precisely so a small switch gets a real floor; at 4, half the panel's keys could be deleted (or the switch restructured) and the guard would still pass. The two floors that shipped for updateBoard/updateDrill (8 against ~23 and ~18) are similarly loose but were the pre-existing shared value; this new case is the one being introduced.
issues.proposed_solution: AGENT-FIXABLE. Raise the updateSessions floor to 8 (its actual parsed key count) and fix the case comment to enumerate keys rather than groups: `floor: 8, // esc q up k down j R K - the switch's real key count`. Optionally tighten updateBoard/updateDrill toward their real counts in the same pass, and delete the contradictory "only ~8" clause from the block comment.
issues.fix_summary: updateSessions floor raised to 8 (the switch's real key count) and both comments rewritten to the per-case real-count rule - no self-contradiction. VERIFIED round 2: key_help_sync_test.go:109 reads `floor: 8, // esc q up k down j R K - the switch's real key count`, and the block comment at :112-120 now says the floor is per-case, set to each switch's real key count (or a safe margin under it) - the "only ~8" clause is gone. MUTATION re-run in the sandbox (dropped the `j` alias from updateSessions' down case): TestBoardKeyHelpInSync FAILS with "parsed only 7 keys from updateSessions ([esc q up k down R K])". The floor now sits exactly at the real count, so any key loss trips it.

issues.title: Nothing pins the sessions panel's status LINE: deleting the status render from viewSessions keeps the whole tui suite green (code-review-standards #8)
issues.description:
cli/internal/tui/view.go:244-246 is the only place the panel surfaces `m.status`:
  `if m.status != "" { b = append(b, "", m.renderStatus(m.status)) }`
Every named refusal this feature adds to the panel reaches the user through those three lines - the new zero-drivable `R` refusal (REV-003's fix), "no live gogo-* session to re-assign" / "...to close", the already-bound refusal, and the green "re-assigned X -> Y" / "closed X" confirmations. Mutation-verified in a sandbox copy of the repo: deleting that block leaves `go test -count=1 ./internal/tui/` fully green, while the user-visible effect is a panel that silently swallows every message its handlers write. Every panel test - including the two the fix round added - asserts `m.status` / `m.statusLevel` only; the two View() assertions that exist (TestSessionsPanelAlwaysOpens) check the empty-list REASON lines, which come from a different branch of viewSessions. This is code-review-standards.md check #8 verbatim ("any user-visible field a handler sets must actually be rendered by the mode's View() ... flag a status/hint that no View() path renders, and a test that asserts only Model.status (not the View() output) for such a path - that gap shipped a silent no-op once (the drill-card status line)"). The production code is CORRECT today; the defect is that nothing stops the next edit from removing it, on the exact surface this feature introduces.
issues.proposed_solution: AGENT-FIXABLE. One line closes it: in TestSessionsPanelReassign/zero_drivable_items_refuses_with_a_named_reason (sessions_panel_test.go:228-246), also assert the message reaches the screen - `if !strings.Contains(m.View(), "no drivable work item") { t.Errorf("the refusal never reaches the panel:\n%s", m.View()) }`. That pins BOTH the wording and viewSessions' status render in one assertion. Re-run the mutation (delete the `if m.status != ""` block from viewSessions) and confirm the test now fails.
issues.fix_summary: Zero-drivable subtest now also asserts the refusal appears in m.View() — the panel's status render leg is pinned.

issues.title: The new Cancel-option subtest asserts the outcome, not the reason: dropping the adoptCancel sentinel from finishReassignSession keeps the suite green
issues.description: sessions_panel_test.go:208-224 ("the Cancel option returns to the panel", added by the fix round for REV-005) asserts only `m.mode == modeSessions` and `len(rr.calls) == 0`. Both hold on the FAILURE path too: if the `sel == adoptCancel` sentinel check is lost, the selection falls through to the feature lookup, no feature matches the sentinel key, and finishReassignSession (session_ops.go:500-503) takes `m.statusBlocked("that work item is no longer present - nothing renamed")` - same mode, same zero renames, amber instead of the neutral "cancelled". Mutation-verified in the sandbox: changing session_ops.go:489 to `if sel == "" || session == "" {` leaves `go test -count=1 ./internal/tui/` fully green, so a deliberate Cancel would start reporting a phantom missing work item with nobody noticing. code-review-standards.md #11(c) requires the assertion to name the exact reason, not just the outcome. Small - the wrong outcome is a misleading status word, not a wrong action - hence a nit, but it is a one-line close on a subtest written this round precisely to pin that door.
issues.proposed_solution: AGENT-FIXABLE. Add the reason to the same subtest: `if m.status != "cancelled" { t.Errorf("Cancel option status = %q, want the neutral cancelled (not the not-found refusal)", m.status) }` (optionally also `m.statusLevel == statusLevelOK`). Re-run the mutation (drop `|| sel == adoptCancel` from finishReassignSession) and confirm the subtest fails.
issues.fix_summary: Cancel-option subtest asserts m.status == "cancelled" — the sentinel branch is pinned against the fall-through amber.

issues.title: gogo-session-update's collision snippet still mints from the RAW slug, contradicting the capped-label rule the REV-006 fix just added three lines above it
issues.description:
The round-2 fix to skills/gogo-session-update/SKILL.md step 5 (lines 77-83) states the contract correctly: cap the SANITIZED slug at 48 (`launch.MaxSessionLabel`), dash-boundary rule and all. But the bash block immediately below it - the operative, copy-pasteable half an executing LLM will actually run - re-derives the name from the raw slug variable:
  `new="gogo-${action}-${slug}"`  (skills/gogo-session-update/SKILL.md:89)
For a work-item slug longer than 48 characters the snippet mints an UNCAPPED name while `launch.sessionName` (launch.go:740) mints the capped one - the two doors then disagree on the name they mint for the same item, which is exactly the FR10 divergence REV-006 exists to close (`SessionMatchesSlug` accepts both candidates, launch.go:808-826, so attribution survives, but the same slug can end up with one CLI-minted and one skill-minted name). Narrow: gogo-plan's slug derivation has no length bound (skills/gogo-plan/SKILL.md:63), yet nothing in this repo exceeds 37 chars - hence minor per the severity guide's "an example that no longer matches", not major.
issues.proposed_solution: AGENT-FIXABLE. Make the snippet consume step 5's computed label instead of the raw slug: name the capped value in the prose (e.g. `label=<the sanitized, capped slug>`) and change the block's first line to `new="gogo-${action}-${label}"`, leaving the has-session / suffix loop untouched. One line, and it removes the last place the skill and launch.sessionName can disagree.
issues.fix_summary: The collision-check bash mints from the capped label ($label, with the past-24 dash note) instead of the raw slug — the skill and launch.sessionName can no longer mint different names.
